title: Container Apps Scaling and Dapr
description: Configure scaling rules for Container Apps and use Dapr to add microservices capabilities without writing extra code.

data.text: Azure Container Apps supports multiple scaling triggers. You can scale based on HTTP traffic, CPU/memory metrics, or external event sources like message queues.

items: HTTP scaling - scale based on concurrent requests
CPU/memory scaling - scale based on resource utilization
Custom scaling via KEDA - scale from any event source (queues, Kafka, databases)

data.title: Azure CLI - Configure Scaling Rules
data.content:
# Scale based on HTTP traffic (min 1, max 10 instances, 50 concurrent requests each)
az containerapp update \
  --name myapp \
  --resource-group myRG \
  --min-replicas 1 \
  --max-replicas 10 \
  --scale-rule-name http-rule \
  --scale-rule-type http \
  --scale-rule-metadata concurrentRequests=50

data.text: Dapr (Distributed Application Runtime) is a portable, event-driven runtime that simplifies building microservices. In Container Apps, Dapr is enabled per-app with a single configuration flag.

items: Service-to-service invocation - call other services with retries and mTLS
State management - key-value stores with Redis, PostgreSQL, or Azure Blob
Pub/Sub - message publishing with Azure Service Bus, Kafka, or RabbitMQ
Secrets management - retrieve secrets from Azure Key Vault

data.title: Azure CLI - Enable Dapr on a Container App
data.content:
# Create or update a Container App with Dapr enabled
az containerapp update \
  --name myapp \
  --resource-group myRG \
  --enable-dapr true \
  --dapr-app-id myapp \
  --dapr-app-port 8080

data.title: Dapr Building Blocks
data.text: Dapr provides building blocks, not frameworks. You can use one, some, or all of them. Each building block exposes a consistent API regardless of the underlying component.

data.caption: Dapr building blocks in a microservices architecture
data.definition:
flowchart TB
    S1[Service A] -->|Dapr Invoke| S2[Service B]
    S1 -->|Dapr Pub| MQ[Message Broker]
    MQ -->|Dapr Sub| S2
    S1 -->|Dapr State| KV[(State Store)]
    S2 -->|Dapr State| KV
    S1 -->|Dapr Secrets| Vault[(Key Vault)]
    S2 -->|Dapr Secrets| Vault

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Scale Container Apps based on HTTP, metrics, or KEDA event sources
Dapr adds microservices capabilities without custom code
Dapr building blocks cover invocation, state, pub/sub, and secrets
Enable Dapr per-app with the --enable-dapr flag
data.takeaway: Scaling and Dapr together make Container Apps a powerful microservices platform.
